reuse.why: Creates a new getExpectedScheduleAmount beside the already-exported getScheduledAmount instead of extending it, re-types the 7.5% formula instead of calling the shared getApproxNumberThreshold, and the API model does not call the new helper at all.

duplication.why: The approximate tolerance duplicates getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.ts, and api-models.ts carries its own inline range resolution (now diverging from the helper's lowest-value rule and ignoring isapprox).

placement.why: The new helper sits in shared/schedules.ts next to the other schedule amount logic and four consumers route through it, but the API model keeps its rule inline.

scope.why: Edits are on-topic; the expected-amount sites in schedule-template.ts and getScheduledAmount (used by SchedulesTable) are left on the old midpoint rule rather than out-of-scope edits being added.

maintainability.why: There are now three definitions of a schedule's expected amount (getExpectedScheduleAmount, getScheduledAmount, the api-models inline ternary) plus the template's own midpoint, so the next rule change will again miss sites.

bypasses_abstraction.where: api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal computes expectedAmount inline instead of calling getExpectedScheduleAmount; getExpectedScheduleAmount re-implements getApproxNumberThreshold; getScheduledAmount in shared/schedules.ts is left as a parallel helper

disguised_duplication.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount's Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075) restates getApproxNumberThreshold under another name; api-models.ts reshapes the range rule as an abs-comparison ternary

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount gains an op parameter and an isapprox branch; api-models.ts expectedAmount and budget/schedule-template.ts scheduleAmount compute the expected amount without it (and getScheduledAmount remains a parallel definition)
